::: {.callout-note}
This document covers the complete setup and workflow for using **VS Code** and **Claude Code**
in `forestsearch` R package development, with explicit notes on differences between
**Linux (System76 / COSMIC)** and **macOS**. All workflows are grounded in the
`forestsearch` architecture: survival endpoints, GLM extensions, `doFuture`/`foreach`
parallelism, and CRAN compliance requirements.
:::

---

# Overview

`forestsearch` is a multi-file CRAN R package with an active GLM extension
(`feature/glm-extension` branch). The development environment combines:

- **RStudio** — primary R editing, package checking, interactive sessions
- **VS Code** — secondary editor for multi-file navigation, terminal management,
  Quarto authoring
- **Claude Code** — AI pair-programmer operating on the repo at the shell level,
  reading and editing files directly
- **GitHub Desktop + RStudio Terminal** — version control

This guide focuses on the VS Code + Claude Code layer and how it complements the
existing RStudio workflow.

---

# Installation

## Node.js (Required for Claude Code)

Claude Code is an npm package and requires Node.js ≥ 18.

### Linux (System76 / COSMIC)

```bash
# Check current version
node --version

# If missing or < 18, install via nvm (recommended over apt)
curl -o- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm/v0.39.7/install.sh | bash

# Reload shell, then:
nvm install --lts
nvm use --lts
node --version   # should print v20.x or v22.x
```

::: {.callout-tip}
**Linux-specific:** `apt install nodejs` often installs Node 12 (Ubuntu 22.04) or
Node 18 (Ubuntu 24.04). Use `nvm` to guarantee a current LTS version regardless of
your Ubuntu release.
:::

### macOS

```bash
# Recommended: use Homebrew
brew install node

# Or use nvm (same as Linux)
curl -o- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm/v0.39.7/install.sh | bash
source ~/.zshrc
nvm install --lts
```

::: {.callout-note}
**macOS vs Linux:** On macOS, Node installed via Homebrew is immediately on `PATH`
without shell restarts. On Linux with `nvm`, you must source `~/.bashrc` or open
a new terminal before `node` and `npm` are available.
:::

## Claude Code

```bash
# Both platforms
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code

# Verify installation
claude --version
```

### Authentication

```bash
# On first run, opens browser for Anthropic login
claude

# Or set API key directly (useful for CI / remote machines)
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-..."
```

**Linux note:** If running on a headless server or in a Wayland session where
browser auto-open fails, Claude Code will print a URL to the terminal — paste it
manually into Firefox.

**macOS note:** Browser opens automatically in your default browser (Safari or
Chrome). No special handling needed.

## VS Code

### Linux (System76 / COSMIC)

Download the `.deb` package from [code.visualstudio.com](https://code.visualstudio.com/):

```bash
# Install from downloaded .deb
sudo dpkg -i code_*.deb
sudo apt-get install -f   # fix any dependency issues

# Or via Snap (easier updates, slight startup overhead)
sudo snap install --classic code
```

::: {.callout-warning}
**COSMIC desktop note:** VS Code renders correctly under COSMIC (X11 compatibility
layer). If you observe blurry fonts, add `--enable-features=UseOzonePlatform
--ozone-platform=wayland` to your VS Code launch flags in
`~/.config/code-flags.conf`.
:::

### macOS

Download the `.zip` or `.dmg` from [code.visualstudio.com](https://code.visualstudio.com/)
and drag to `/Applications`. Then enable the `code` CLI:

- Open VS Code → `Cmd+Shift+P` → **Shell Command: Install 'code' command in PATH**

# VS Code Configuration for `forestsearch`

## Required Extensions

Install these from the VS Code Extensions panel (`Ctrl+Shift+X` / `Cmd+Shift+X`):

| Extension ID | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `REditorSupport.r` | R syntax highlighting, linting, hover docs |
| `quarto.quarto` | `.qmd` rendering, preview, syntax |
| `eamodio.gitlens` | Branch visibility, blame, history |
| `mechatroner.rainbow-csv` | Readable `.csv` inspection |
| `ms-vscode.live-server` | Preview rendered HTML (optional) |
| `christian-kohler.path-intellisense` | File path autocomplete |

## Workspace Settings

Create `.vscode/settings.json` in the `forestsearch` repo root:

```json
{
  "r.rterm.linux": "/usr/bin/radian",
  "r.rterm.mac": "/usr/local/bin/radian",
  "r.bracketedPaste": true,
  "r.sessionWatcher": true,
  "editor.formatOnSave": false,
  "editor.rulers": [80],
  "editor.tabSize": 2,
  "files.associations": {
    "*.R": "r",
    "*.r": "r",
    "*.qmd": "quarto",
    "*.Rmd": "rmd"
  },
  "files.exclude": {
    "**/.git": true,
    "**/node_modules": true,
    "**/*.Rcheck": true,
    "**/man/*.Rd": false
  },
  "[r]": {
    "editor.defaultFormatter": "REditorSupport.r",
    "editor.formatOnSave": false
  },
  "terminal.integrated.defaultProfile.linux": "bash",
  "terminal.integrated.defaultProfile.osx": "zsh"
}
```

::: {.callout-note}
**Platform difference:** `r.rterm.linux` and `r.rterm.mac` take separate paths.
On macOS with Homebrew, radian is typically at `/opt/homebrew/bin/radian` (Apple
Silicon) or `/usr/local/bin/radian` (Intel). Run `which radian` on both platforms
to confirm the correct path.
:::

## Radian (Better R Console)

```bash
# Linux
pip3 install radian --user

# macOS (Homebrew Python)
pip3 install radian

# Verify
which radian
radian --version
```

# The `CLAUDE.md` File — Most Important Setup Step

Claude Code reads `CLAUDE.md` from the repo root automatically at the start of
every session. This encodes all `forestsearch`-specific architectural constraints
so you never have to re-explain them.

Create `CLAUDE.md` at the repo root with the following content:

````markdown
# forestsearch Development Context

## Package Identity
- CRAN R package for subgroup identification in clinical trials
- Active branch: `feature/glm-extension` (binary/continuous GLM extension)
- Style guide: tidyverse style guide throughout
- Documentation: roxygen2; `devtools::document()` overwrites NAMESPACE
- CRAN check pipeline: `devtools::document()` → `devtools::load_all()` → `devtools::check()`

## Critical File Rules
- **File-first:** Always read the current file before producing any revision.
  Never produce revisions that don't incorporate the author's own edits.
- **Quarto is intentional:** Never convert `.qmd` to `.Rmd`.
- **Scope discipline:** When asked about a Quarto document, do not touch R source
  files, DESCRIPTION, NAMESPACE, or pkgdown config unless explicitly asked.
- **NAMESPACE is generated:** Never hand-edit NAMESPACE. Use `@export` tags in
  roxygen2 headers and run `devtools::document()`.

## Branch Strategy
- `master`: CRAN-ready; must pass `devtools::check()` with 0 errors/warnings/notes
- `feature/glm-extension`: Active GLM development (binary + continuous outcomes)
- `cran-review-N`: Reviewer response branches; squash-merged to master

## Known Architectural Debts
- Line 720 of `forestsearch_main.R`: `merge(by = "id")` hardcodes `id_name` — known debt
- Four `\dontrun{}` blocks remain in `oc_analyses_gbsg.R`
- `subset()` in programming contexts is fragile — prefer `[` or `filter()`

## Silent Failure Risks (highest priority in code review)
- `.errorhandling = "remove"` with no post-hoc accounting → silent task loss
- `valid_pnames` whitelist in `.run_fs_analysis_gen()` silently drops unrecognized params
- `tryCatch` silently catching degenerate survival objects

## Parallel Architecture (`doFuture` / `foreach`)
- Functions called inside `%dofuture%` bodies must be explicitly exported or embedded
- `future::plan("sequential")` must be set inside worker bodies to prevent nested parallelism
- `devtools::install()` required for `callr` workers — `load_all()` is insufficient
- Nested parallelism bug root cause: `valid_pnames` whitelist silently drops params

## GLM Extension (v0.2.0, `feature/glm-extension`)
Key new files:
- `glm_effect_estimators.R` — estimator closure factory (`make_effect_estimator()`)
- `glm_effect_profile.R` — GLM effect profile
- `grf_subg_harm_glm.R` — main GLM entry point (`grf.subg.harm.glm`)
- `plot_sg_glm_outcomes.R` — GLM outcome visualization
- `glm_spline_fit.R` — GLM spline support

Parameter: `outcome_type` ∈ {"binary", "survival", "continuous"}
Effect measures: "OR", "RR", "RD" (binary); "HR", "AHR" (survival); "MD" (continuous)

## Quarto Calibration Suite
Five documents in `quarto/`:
- `calibration_binary_leff.qmd`
- `calibration_survival_fourway.qmd`
- `calibration_survival_leff_grid.qmd`
- `selection_binary_frontier.qmd`
- `selection_survival_frontier.qmd`

All parameters consolidated in setup chunks. `_quarto.yml` centralizes formatting.
Git tracks `quarto/_output/` HTML and `quarto/_data/` `.rds` bundles (simulations expensive).

## Code Review Protocol
Structure audits by severity: Critical → High → Moderate → Minor.
Audit ALL instances across ALL files before proposing any fix.
Never address errors one at a time as they surface.
````

::: {.callout-tip}
**Why this matters:** Without `CLAUDE.md`, Claude Code starts each session with zero
knowledge of your architecture. With it, constraints like "don't hand-edit NAMESPACE"
and "audit all files before fixing" are enforced automatically from the first prompt.
:::

# Launching Claude Code

## Standard Session Start

```bash
# Navigate to repo root
cd ~/path/to/forestsearch

# Confirm branch
git branch   # should show * feature/glm-extension (or master)

# Launch Claude Code
claude
```

Claude Code will print the repo name and confirm it has read `CLAUDE.md`.

## Branch-Oriented Session Start

Always orient Claude Code at session start when your work is branch-specific:

```
> We are on the feature/glm-extension branch. The files glm_effect_estimators.R,
  grf_subg_harm_glm.R, plot_sg_glm_outcomes.R, and glm_spline_fit.R are
  GLM-extension files not present on master. Keep all edits scoped to these files
  unless I explicitly say otherwise.
```

---

# Terminal Layout in VS Code

VS Code supports split terminals. The recommended layout for `forestsearch` work:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  VS Code Editor Pane                                │
│  (open: glm_effect_estimators.R + CLAUDE.md side   │
│   by side, or .qmd + _output/ HTML)                │
├──────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┤
│  Terminal 1          │  Terminal 2                  │
│  Claude Code session │  radian / R session          │
│  $ claude            │  $ radian                    │
│                      │  > devtools::load_all()       │
└──────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────┘
```

Open a split terminal: `` Ctrl+` `` to open terminal → click the split icon (⊞)
in the terminal toolbar.

::: {.callout-note}
**macOS shortcut:** `` Ctrl+` `` works on both platforms. On macOS you can also
use `Cmd+J` to toggle the terminal panel.
:::

# Common Claude Code Prompt Patterns

## File Reading (Always First)

The most important rule: **always read the file before revising it.**

```
> Read glm_effect_estimators.R and show me the current structure of
  make_effect_estimator().
```

```
> Before making any changes: read forestsearch_main.R lines 710-730
  and confirm how id_name is currently handled.
```

## Cross-File Audits

Claude Code can grep and read across all 55+ `.R` files:

```
> Audit all .R files for uses of merge(by = "id") and report which ones
  ignore the id_name argument. Organize findings by severity.
```

```
> Find all %dofuture% blocks across the package and list every variable
  referenced inside them that is not passed via .export or embedded.
  This is a parallel scoping audit.
```

```
> Find all tryCatch() calls that catch errors silently (no message,
  no warning, just return(NULL) or NA). List file and line number for each.
```

## CRAN Compliance Checks

```
> Scan all .R files for non-ASCII characters. List file, line number,
  and the offending character.
```

```
> List every function that appears in NAMESPACE but does not have
  an @export tag in its roxygen2 header. Also list functions with
  @export tags that are missing from NAMESPACE.
```

```
> Find all \dontrun{} blocks in the package and list their locations.
  Suggest which can be converted to \donttest{}.
```

## Targeted Edits

```
> In glm_effect_estimators.R, add input validation for the effect_measure
  argument. Valid values are "OR", "RR", "RD" for binary; "HR", "AHR"
  for survival; "MD" for continuous. Follow the validation pattern used
  in Cox_estimation_helpers.R for the est.scale argument.
  Read both files before making any change.
```

# Platform Differences: Linux vs macOS

## Path Conventions

| Item | Linux (System76) | macOS |
|---|---|---|
| R binary | `/usr/bin/R` | `/usr/local/bin/R` (Intel) or `/opt/homebrew/bin/R` (Apple Silicon) |
| radian | `~/.local/bin/radian` | `/usr/local/bin/radian` or `/opt/homebrew/bin/radian` |
| Node / npm | `~/.nvm/versions/node/...` (nvm) | `/opt/homebrew/bin/node` (brew) |
| Claude Code | `~/.nvm/.../bin/claude` | `/opt/homebrew/bin/claude` |
| Home directory | `/home/larry` | `/Users/larry` |
| Config files | `~/.bashrc`, `~/.bash_profile` | `~/.zshrc` (default shell is zsh since macOS Catalina) |

## Shell Differences

Linux uses **bash** by default; macOS uses **zsh** since Catalina (2019).

```bash
# Linux: add to ~/.bashrc
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-..."
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

# macOS: add to ~/.zshrc
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-..."
export PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH"
```

After editing:
```bash
# Linux
source ~/.bashrc

# macOS
source ~/.zshrc
```

## Parallel Computing (`doFuture` / `multicore`)

::: {.callout-warning}
**Critical platform difference for `forestsearch` parallel code.**
:::

```r
# multicore forking works on Linux
future::plan("multicore", workers = 4)   # ✅ Linux: TRUE fork-based parallelism

# On macOS: multicore is disabled in RStudio (GUI process restriction)
future::plan("multicore", workers = 4)   # ⚠️  macOS + RStudio → silently falls back to sequential
future::plan("multisession", workers = 4) # ✅ macOS: use multisession instead
```

When testing `bootstrap_dofuture_main.R` on macOS, always use `multisession`:

```r
# Safe cross-platform plan for forestsearch bootstrap
plan_str <- if (.Platform$OS.type == "unix" && !grepl("darwin", R.version$os)) {
  "multicore"
} else {
  "multisession"
}
future::plan(plan_str, workers = parallel::detectCores() - 1)
```

## File System Performance

- **Linux:** File I/O inside `%dofuture%` workers is fast; `.rds` bundle writes
  in `quarto/_data/` are near-instant.
- **macOS:** File I/O can be slower due to Gatekeeper and SIP; large `.rds`
  writes (>100 MB) may be noticeably slower. This matters when running the
  calibration Quarto documents that save expensive simulation outputs.

## `devtools::check()` Behavior

```r
# Linux: check() runs in a subprocess using the system R
devtools::check()  # uses /usr/bin/R by default

# macOS: check() may use a different R than your interactive session
# if multiple R versions are installed via Homebrew or CRAN pkg
# Confirm which R is active:
system("which R")
R.home()
```

On macOS, if you have multiple R versions via [rig](https://github.com/r-lib/rig),
set the active version explicitly:

```bash
rig default 4.4   # or whichever version you're targeting
```

## win-builder (CRAN Submission) — Both Platforms

Both Linux and macOS require the same `win-builder` submission step for CRAN:

```r
devtools::check_win_devel()   # submits to win-builder; results emailed ~30 min
devtools::check_win_release()
```

There is no platform difference here — win-builder runs on Windwows regardless of
your development OS.

# Worked Workflow Examples

## Workflow 1: Revising GLM Simulations with Debug-First Strategy

This is the recommended pattern when you have modified GLM simulation code and want
to validate behavior **before** installing the package.

### Context

You have edited `glm_effect_estimators.R` and `grf_subg_harm_glm.R` on
`feature/glm-extension`. You want to test `grf.subg.harm.glm()` with a small
binary-outcome dataset before running `devtools::install()`.

### Step 1 — Orient Claude Code

```
> We are on the feature/glm-extension branch working on the GLM simulation
  calibration. The relevant files are:
    - glm_effect_estimators.R   (estimator closures)
    - grf_subg_harm_glm.R       (main GLM entry point)
    - calibration_binary_leff.qmd (Quarto calibration doc)

  Please read grf_subg_harm_glm.R now and summarize the current
  argument signature of grf.subg.harm.glm().
```

### Step 2 — Load with `load_all()` for Interactive Debugging

In Terminal 2 (radian):

```r
library(devtools)
load_all()   # loads package from source WITHOUT installing
             # changes to .R files are immediately reflected

# Construct a minimal binary outcome dataset
set.seed(42)
n <- 200
df_test <- data.frame(
  y      = rbinom(n, 1, 0.3),
  trt    = rbinom(n, 1, 0.5),
  age    = rnorm(n, 55, 10),
  biomarker = rnorm(n, 0, 1),
  id     = seq_len(n)
)

# Test the GLM entry point
result <- grf.subg.harm.glm(
  y          = df_test$y,
  trt        = df_test$trt,
  X          = df_test[, c("age", "biomarker")],
  df         = df_test,
  outcome_type = "binary",
  effect_measure = "OR",
  n.boots    = 50,   # small for debugging
  details    = TRUE
)
```

::: {.callout-tip}
**Why `load_all()` not `install()`?** `devtools::load_all()` sources all package
functions into the global environment without compiling or installing. Changes
to `.R` files take effect on the next `load_all()` call — no install/restart
cycle. This is the correct tool for iterative debugging.

**Exception:** `callr`-based parallel workers (as used in `bootstrap_dofuture_main.R`)
require the package to be *installed*, not just loaded. For those, you must use
`devtools::install()` before testing parallel code.
:::

### Step 3 — Ask Claude Code to Diagnose Errors

If Step 2 produces an error, paste it into Claude Code:

```
> grf.subg.harm.glm() is failing with this error when outcome_type = "binary":

  Error in make_effect_estimator(outcome_type, effect_measure) :
    unused argument (effect_measure = "OR")

  Read glm_effect_estimators.R and diagnose the root cause. Do not
  propose a fix yet — just explain what is wrong.
```

After diagnosis:

```
> Now propose the minimal fix. Show the exact str_replace you would
  apply to glm_effect_estimators.R. Do not touch any other file.
```

### Step 4 — Reload and Re-test

After Claude Code applies the fix:

```r
# In radian terminal
load_all()   # pick up the edit immediately

result <- grf.subg.harm.glm(
  y = df_test$y, trt = df_test$trt,
  X = df_test[, c("age", "biomarker")], df = df_test,
  outcome_type = "binary", effect_measure = "OR",
  n.boots = 50, details = TRUE
)

# Inspect output
str(result)
result$fs.est$harm.definition
```

Repeat Steps 3–4 until `result` is correct.

### Step 5 — Install and Test Parallel Bootstrap

Only after interactive debugging passes:

```r
# Install (needed for callr workers in bootstrap)
devtools::install(quiet = TRUE)

# Test parallel bootstrap (small scale)
library(forestsearch)

boot_result <- forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture(
  y = df_test$y, trt = df_test$trt,
  X = df_test[, c("age", "biomarker")], df = df_test,
  outcome_type = "binary", effect_measure = "OR",
  n.boots = 100,
  parallel_args = list(
    plan    = "multisession",   # macOS: use multisession; Linux: multicore OK
    workers = 2
  )
)
```

### Step 6 — Run Full CRAN Check

```r
devtools::document()   # regenerate man/ and NAMESPACE
devtools::check()      # full check; must pass with 0 errors/warnings/notes
```

## Workflow 2: Cross-File Audit Before a CRAN Submission

### Context

You are preparing `v0.2.0` for CRAN submission and want a systematic audit
of the GLM extension before running win-builder.

### Step 1 — Namespace and Export Audit

```
> Audit the GLM extension for CRAN submission readiness.

  Step 1: Read NAMESPACE and list every grf.subg.harm.glm-related
  function that is exported.

  Step 2: Read grf_subg_harm_glm.R, glm_effect_estimators.R,
  plot_sg_glm_outcomes.R, and glm_cs_fit (wherever it lives).
  List every function that has an @export tag.

  Step 3: Report any functions with @export tags NOT in NAMESPACE,
  and any NAMESPACE entries with no @export tag. Organize by severity.
```

### Step 2 — Silent Failure Audit

```
> Audit the GLM extension files (glm_effect_estimators.R,
  grf_subg_harm_glm.R, bootstrap_dofuture_main.R) specifically for
  silent failure patterns:

  1. tryCatch blocks that return NULL or NA without any message
  2. .errorhandling = "remove" in %dofuture% / %dopar% calls
  3. Any use of suppressWarnings() or suppressMessages() that could
     hide structural problems

  Report file, line number, and the specific risk for each instance.
  Do not propose fixes — audit only.
```

### Step 3 — Non-ASCII and Encoding Check

Claude Code can run shell commands:

```
> Run this shell command and show the output:
  grep -rn --include="*.R" '[^\x00-\x7F]' R/
```

Or ask Claude Code directly:

```
> Scan all .R files for non-ASCII characters. For each occurrence,
  report the file, line number, the character, and its Unicode code point.
```

### Step 4 — Fix in Priority Order

```
> Now address the issues found, in this order:
  1. Missing @export tags (NAMESPACE divergence)
  2. Silent tryCatch blocks in GLM bootstrap path
  3. Non-ASCII characters

  Read each file before editing. Apply one fix at a time and confirm
  before proceeding to the next.
```

### Step 5 — Final Check Sequence

```r
devtools::document()
devtools::load_all()
devtools::check()

# If clean:
devtools::check_win_devel()
```

---

## Workflow 3: Quarto Calibration Document Revision

### Context

You are revising `calibration_binary_leff.qmd` — updating the simulation grid
or fixing a parameter that was incorrectly scattered outside the setup chunk.

### Step 1 — Orient Claude Code (Scope Discipline)

```
> I am working on calibration_binary_leff.qmd in the quarto/ directory.

  Scope rule for this session: do NOT touch any .R source files,
  DESCRIPTION, NAMESPACE, or pkgdown config. Work only on the .qmd file
  and, if necessary, _quarto.yml.

  Please read calibration_binary_leff.qmd now and identify every
  tunable parameter that is NOT in the setup chunk.
  List them with their line numbers.
```

### Step 2 — Parameter Consolidation

```
> Consolidate all tunable parameters into the setup chunk.
  The parameters that should be there are:

    n_sims, n_min_vec, leff_grid, outcome_type, effect_measure,
    calibration_seed, output_dir

  Move any of these that appear outside the setup chunk INTO the setup
  chunk. Use the existing setup chunk variable names consistently.
  Show me the revised setup chunk before applying any change.
```

### Step 3 — Preview Without Re-running Simulations

Quarto documents that load from `_data/*.rds` can be previewed cheaply:

```bash
# In Terminal 1 (bash)
cd quarto
quarto preview calibration_binary_leff.qmd --no-execute-daemon
```

This renders using cached `.rds` data without re-running simulations.

To force full re-execution (expensive — re-runs all simulations):

```bash
quarto render calibration_binary_leff.qmd
```

### Step 4 — Git Tracking for Output

After a successful render:

```bash
git add quarto/_output/calibration_binary_leff.html
git add quarto/_data/leff_calibration_binary.rds
git commit -m "feat: update binary leff calibration grid"
```

::: {.callout-note}
**Why track outputs in Git?** Simulation outputs are expensive to regenerate.
Tracking the `.rds` bundles and rendered HTML in Git means collaborators (or
future-you) can load pre-computed results without re-running hours of simulation.
The `^quarto$` entry in `.Rbuildignore` prevents these from leaking into the
CRAN tarball.
:::

---

## Workflow 4: Debugging Parallel Bootstrap on macOS

### Context

The `bootstrap_dofuture_main.R` parallel bootstrap is failing silently — workers
complete but results are empty — when running on macOS.

### Step 1 — Confirm the Plan Setting

```
> Read bootstrap_dofuture_main.R and show me exactly where
  future::plan() is set. Is it set inside or outside the worker body?
  What plan value is used?
```

### Step 2 — Switch to Sequential for Diagnosis

```r
# In radian — bypass parallelism entirely
devtools::load_all()

boot_result <- forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture(
  ...,
  parallel_args = list(plan = "sequential", workers = 1)
)
```

If sequential works but parallel fails → parallel scoping issue.

### Step 3 — Identify Unexported Variables

```
> In bootstrap_dofuture_main.R, list every variable and function
  referenced inside %dofuture% worker bodies that is not:
  (a) passed via .export = c(...), or
  (b) a base R function, or
  (c) defined inside the worker body itself.

  This is a parallel scoping audit. Report all missing exports.
```

### Step 4 — Add Missing Exports

```
> The following objects are missing from .export:
    make_effect_estimator, .run_single_consistency_split, estimator_fn

  Add them to the .export vector in the %dofuture% call in
  bootstrap_dofuture_main.R. Read the file first.
```

### Step 5 — macOS-Specific: Force `multisession`

```
> In bootstrap_dofuture_main.R, update the plan selection logic so that
  on macOS (R.version$os containing "darwin"), the plan always falls
  back to "multisession" even if "multicore" was requested.
  Add a message() call informing the user of the fallback.
```

## Branch Switching

```bash
# In the bash terminal (not via Claude Code — safer to do manually)
git checkout master
git checkout feature/glm-extension
```

::: {.callout-warning}
Avoid asking Claude Code to switch branches mid-session. The file system
changes instantly and Claude Code's in-memory context of the files may
become stale. Switch branches in the bash terminal, then start a new
Claude Code session.
:::

# Troubleshooting

## Claude Code Can't Find `R`

```bash
# Linux
which R        # if blank: R is not on PATH
sudo ln -s /usr/lib/R/bin/R /usr/local/bin/R  # or add to .bashrc

# macOS
which R        # if blank:
export PATH="/usr/local/bin:$PATH"  # Intel
export PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH"  # Apple Silicon
```

## `devtools::install()` Required for Parallel Workers

If Claude Code suggests testing parallel bootstrap with just `load_all()`:

```
> CORRECTION: The parallel bootstrap uses callr workers which require
  the package to be installed, not just loaded. The correct sequence is:
    devtools::document()
    devtools::install(quiet = TRUE)
    library(forestsearch)
  then test the parallel function.
```

## Claude Code Edits the Wrong File

If Claude Code starts editing a file outside the declared scope:

```
> STOP. You are editing [wrong file]. The scope for this session is
  [correct file] only. Revert that edit and re-read the scope rule.
```

## `future::plan("multicore")` Falls Back Silently on macOS

```r
# Check what plan is actually active
future::plan()   # prints current plan; look for SequentialFuture if fallen back
```

If you see `SequentialFuture` when you expected `MulticoreFuture`, switch to
`multisession` explicitly (see Workflow 4).

# Quick Reference Card

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  forestsearch: VS Code + Claude Code Quick Reference            │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  ALWAYS before editing:   read the file first                   │
│  ALWAYS for NAMESPACE:    @export tags + devtools::document()   │
│  ALWAYS for parallel:     devtools::install() not load_all()    │
│  ALWAYS on macOS:         plan("multisession") not "multicore"  │
│  NEVER:                   convert .qmd to .Rmd                  │
│  NEVER:                   hand-edit NAMESPACE                    │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Debug sequence:          load_all() → test → fix → load_all()  │
│  Install sequence:        document() → install() → library()    │
│  CRAN check:              document() → load_all() → check()     │
│  Parallel test:           document() → install() → test         │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Linux parallel plan:     "multicore" (fork-based, RStudio OK)  │
│  macOS parallel plan:     "multisession" (RStudio restriction)  │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Git: track quarto/_output/ HTML and quarto/_data/ .rds         │
│  Git: .Rbuildignore has ^quarto$ (keeps CRAN tarball clean)     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
